title: Conditional A2 gradient flow is a deterministic baseline, not the R-192 stochastic production owner
question: Does the current conditional A2 P1 real-L2 gradient flow supply the stochastic/root-labelled production owner required by R-192?
method: Hash-pin and read the live A2 status and pinned functional manifest, including its conditional H2 fixed-torus gradient-flow scope and no-overclaim boundary.
Hash-pin the current R-192 bounded production-cylinder manifest and compare its first failure slot and owner-slot audit against the A2 authority.

finding: A2 supplies a conditional deterministic real-L2 gradient flow for the hash-pinned P1 functional on the fixed torus, with energy decay and smoothing within that theorem. It does not supply stochastic heat, heat_root_incidence, a root-labelled filtration, conditional replicas, a raw-current spatial intertwiner or a production one-use q-ledger. The current R-192 audit therefore remains mapped=false/structural-only at heat_root_incidence. The A2 result is a valid conditional PDE baseline, not a canonical A13 production dynamics owner.
decision_reason: Relabelling a deterministic L2 gradient flow as the stochastic/root-labelled R-192 owner would change the dynamic contract and silently import missing filtration, replica, raw-current and q-ledger data. The exact crosswalk advances candidate selection while preserving the A2 and A13 boundaries.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing owner crosswalk only. No A2 refutation, R-192 completion, A13 closure, Sector-A, Pre-A, physical-empty, OS/KMS, real-time, thermodynamic or continuum conclusion follows.
next_action: Keep the A2 gradient flow as a conditional deterministic baseline. Supply and hash-pin the actual stochastic/root-labelled production map, filtration, conditional replicas, raw-current spatial identity and q-ledger before rerunning R-192.
